headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of grid infrastructure from residential ratepayers to large energy users, potentially decreasing residential utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups (indirectly), Dominion Energy (with amendments).
opponents: Data center developers, large industrial users (initially).
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers and allowing Dominion Energy to spend more on burying distribution lines. This aims to ensure data centers pay their fair share for energy generation and distribution, preventing costs from being unfairly passed to residential customers.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This legislation mandates data centers to report their water usage, aiming for greater transparency regarding environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups (e.g., Potomac Conservancy, Piedmont Environmental Council), local communities concerned about water resources, Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (potentially, due to increased reporting burden).
news_headline: Virginia Data Center Legislation: Tax, Energy & Siting
news_summary: SB 553 requires proposed industrial facilities, including data centers, to submit annual water consumption estimates for rezoning and special use permit decisions. This aims to increase transparency on water use and allow for impact consideration.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes new regulations for data center locations and noise levels, addressing community concerns.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, environmental and conservation groups, neighborhood associations, historic preservation advocates, farmland protection groups, local planning and public health organizations, Del. Joshua Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations, pro-growth business or utility groups (concerned about permitting delays and added costs).
news_headline: What does Data center site assessment and sound profile for high energy use facilities (HB153) do?
news_summary: This bill requires Virginia localities to mandate site assessments for new high energy use facilities (HEUF) over 100 MW, examining sound profiles near homes and schools. Localities can also require assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
